The caterpillar alternates direction, and each fruit he eats is the next one out on the opposite side. Let $d_w$ be the distance of the trip made at weight $w$, and let $t_w$ be its duration. At weight $w$ his speed is $2^{-w}$, so $t_w = d_w \cdot 2^{w}$.

Tracing the trips:

| Weight $w$ | Trip | Distance $d_w$ | Time $t_w = d_w 2^w$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | $0 \to 1$ | 1 | 1 |
| 1 | $1 \to -1$ | 2 | 4 |
| 2 | $-1 \to 2$ | 3 | 12 |
| 3 | $2 \to -3$ | 5 | 40 |
| 4 | $-3 \to 4$ | 7 | 112 |
| 5 | $4 \to -5$ | 9 | 288 |
| 6 | $-5 \to 6$ | 11 | 704 |
| 7 | $6 \to -7$ | 13 | 1664 |
| 8 | $-7 \to 8$ | 15 | 3840 |
| 9 | $8 \to -9$ | 17 | 8704 |

After the trip at weight 9 he eats the fruit at $-9$ and reaches weight 10. The total time is the sum of the times for $w = 0$ through $9$:

$$1 + 4 + 12 + 40 + 112 + 288 + 704 + 1664 + 3840 + 8704 = 15369.$$

So he weighs 10 pounds after 15369 days.

ANSWER: 15369
